//: FILE: examples/new-candidate.json  -  a sample 'add a candidate' request
JSON files cannot contain normal comments, so explanations are stored
in extra entries whose names start with //. The server simply ignores
any entry it does not recognise, so these do no harm.
WHAT THIS FILE IS, IN PLAIN ENGLISH
A ready-made form for adding ONE new candidate, so you don't have to
type the details by hand. You send it to the server with the POST
/candidates request. The server checks it, saves it, and replies with
'201 Created' and the new candidate (who gets the next id, e.g. 16).
HOW TO USE IT (in a second terminal, while 'npm run dev' is running)
(-X POST = send data;  -H = tell the server it is JSON;
Then open http://localhost:3000/jobs/1/matches - Lisbeth now appears
as the 2nd-best Backend Detective (she has 2 of the 3 skills).
Sending the same file twice gives '409 already exists'.
To remove her again: npm run seed
// name: REQUIRED. The person's name. Must not already exist.
name: Lisbeth S.
// availability: REQUIRED. Must be exactly one of: Immediate, 2 weeks, Not looking.
// skills: REQUIRED. A list with at least one skill. New skill words (like 'security') are added to the skills dictionary automatically. Capitals/spaces are tidied: 'Public Speaking' becomes 'public-speaking'.
// traits: OPTIONAL. Personality words. 'autonomous' matches Backend Detective's culture keyword, earning culture points.
quirk: Finds the bug before you finish describing it.
